text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo –  2 To ask the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether he can provide an update on the SPH Media Trust committee’s review of overstated circulation numbers of its publications; and (b) what are the measures that SPH Media Trust and the Government will take to prevent similar incidents in the future.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in respect of the investigation report issued by SPH Media Group’s audit and risk committee on overstated circulation numbers of SPH news publications (a) whether the steps that have been recommended to be undertaken by SPH Media Group in the report are assessed to be adequate; (b) whether regulatory action is being considered; and (c) whether any new regulation is being contemplated to tighten reporting standards by media groups on circulation numbers and other key information to ensure accountability for the same.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in view of the findings and recommendations in the recent report by the Audit and Risk Committee of SPH Media Group, what are the lessons and safeguards that the Ministry will take on funding to SPH Media or other entities in the future.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether there is a need to set up a Committee of Inquiry to reveal the cause of Singapore Press Holdings (SPH)’s overstatement of its daily circulation numbers; (b) whether the Ministry will consider revealing to the public the companies that are involved in assisting SPH to overstate the circulation numbers; and (c) what are the lessons learnt to prevent such occurrences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will also address the Question filed by Ms Hany Soh1 for a future Sitting.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second point is that whatever happened had no bearing on public funds, because the Government did not have a funding relationship with SMT before the end of 2022.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For avoidance of doubt, the first tranche of funding was disbursed in March 2023.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the events preceded the period of funding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Correspondingly, the question of loss of public funds does not arise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, I explained the Government’s reasons for funding SMT’s transformation, which had little to do with circulation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, the Government made it clear that it expected SMT to properly investigate the matter and to give the public a proper account.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT’s Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) has since concluded its investigations and its findings have been extensively reported.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My update to Members will, therefore, focus on three areas, namely, the ARC’s findings; what SMT will do to address the underlying issues; and what the Government will put in place to ensure public funding to SMT remains prudent and accountable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members will have read in media reports, there were three noteworthy findings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is around 10% of overall circulation of their main titles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The ARC did not find any evidence of the involvement of the journalism and editorial departments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, the ARC found that the accounting impact was not deemed to be material to the financial statements of SPH Media Group for the financial year ending August 2022 taken as a whole.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, there were possible offences committed, based on several findings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Consequently, the ARC has recommended that a Police report be filed and the Board has done so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Mr Murali Pillai and Mr Ang Wei Neng’s questions on the specific offences being considered, I am unable to give further details as this is now an ongoing Police investigation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked whether the overstated circulation figures and consequent financial impact have been corrected.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: After SMT was formed in December 2021, it began internally reviewing the data it took over and rectified the inconsistencies detected.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Its accounts since its first financial year ending August 2022 no longer have these inconsistencies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for the period before SMT was formed, these findings have been made public and further actions to deal with the erroneous figures are matters to be decided by the relevant parties involved then.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Hany Soh filed a related question for a future Sitting.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: She asked if NLB had been a subscriber of SPH Media’s publications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: NLB’s subscription provides its members with access to various titles published by SPH Media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Neither the subscription rates nor members’ access are related to circulation numbers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is, therefore, no impact of any kind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how SMT will take up the ARC’s recommendations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT has shared with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) that its follow-up is in three main areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One, they will benchmark their reporting to international standards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are commissioning the World Association of Newspapers and News Publishers (WAN-IFRA) to review and advise on their methods for measuring the reach of various titles.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These are the metrics that the public, businesses and the Government will be concerned with, to know how many people come into contact with a title’s content.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Two, SMT will improve internal controls, including tightening deal structure and pricing approval procedures, such as requirements for approvals at the appropriate levels; strengthening guidelines and checks for revenue and cost recognition; improving separation of duties among staff to ensure data accuracy and accountability; and commissioning external parties to review its governance, control and compliance measures, with the aim of embedding the enhancements into a new enterprise resource planning system.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Three, SMT will enhance its risk management practices throughout the organisation and review its risk culture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT has assured MCI that they will implement these measures immediately and will provide us with regular status updates on a half-yearly basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This leads me to the third set of questions that Members have asked: whether this affects the Government’s funding to SMT.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Reuters Institute Digital News Report is published annually and its 2023 edition released last month is a timely reminder why funding support for mainstream media remains necessary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even with dozens of news sources easily available, audiences in Singapore consistently turn to our mainstream media when they need something they can trust.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Specifically, trust levels in all the SMT’s major titles remained much higher than the global average – 73% of respondents expressed trust in The Straits Times, up three percentage points from last year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is against the backdrop of the erosion of trust in news globally, from an already modest 42% last year to 40% this year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Trusted news media made possible by quality journalism is a public good we cannot afford to compromise on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is more important than ever when the environment is full of disinformation and sensationalised news.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, SMT can only deliver quality journalism if they can continue to strengthen their capabilities and reach audiences in the digital age.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Media consumption has moved online rapidly, disrupting the entire industry.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT must move decisively into the online space.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the new competencies take time to build and the economics of news media in the digital era do not make it easy for newsrooms to survive, let alone fund new investments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The costs of running a professional newsroom remain high, and data and technology infrastructure require substantial upfront costs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Yet, revenue streams are a fraction of what they were in the heyday of print media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Advertising revenue has been squeezed, with a large share going to platforms run by Big Tech.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Growing subscription revenue in a world of free news is also challenging – only 15% of Singapore readers surveyed by Reuters Institute are willing to pay for it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The challenge is even more pronounced for vernacular publications, which have smaller readerships.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are an essential part of our multicultural society and unique identity and give voice to our ethnic communities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government's funding is, ultimately, to fulfil a public good – that of trusted news media enabled through quality journalism.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This does not, however, mean that we have no additional expectations of SMT in light of this incident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We acknowledge their seriousness in investigating the concerns and for making the findings public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As it is now a matter for the Police to consider, we should turn our focus to making sure SMT will discharge its public duties responsibly on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the leadership level, the SMT management and board have demonstrated commitment to changing legacy practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We expect SMT to persist in addressing internal weaknesses and systematically follow up on the required changes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members will recall that the circulation data issue emerged because SMT was conducting its own review and due diligence following the transfer of the media business from SPH Limited in December 2021.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This whole set of findings arose out of SMT's own internal review, which no one in particular asked them to do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They themselves felt it was important to start on a clean slate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT has assured us that it intends to follow up on the ARC's recommendations to ensure organisation-wide accountability and to bring the organisation forward.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We welcome the plans SMT has set in motion, including instituting internationally accepted benchmarks and extensively reviewing its governance and control measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is an ongoing process and MCI will work closely with SMT to ensure these measures are implemented.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Mr Murali's question on reporting standards, the key point is to ensure reports are consistent with international best practice.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is in SMT’s own interest to uphold reporting standards, with or without regulation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Tin and Mr Zhulkarnain asked if we will impose additional safeguards, and Mr Leong asked if we would put in key performance indicators (KPIs) evaluating SMT's improvements in risk management and controls.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These must be agreed upon and SMT is not allowed to change them without MCI's consent; (b) SMT's KPI performance and financial statements must also be audited by independent external auditors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, the evaluation of and improvements to internal processes are clearly the responsibility of SMT's executive team.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government will intervene if there is a case of misconduct or mismanagement of public funding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this regard, we have built in safeguards that allow the Government to conduct our own ad hoc audits.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If serious wrongdoings are found, we have the right to terminate funding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT's ability to address these management issues will be taken into consideration.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The outstanding matter of the Police investigation should be allowed to take its course.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At its conclusion, the follow-up actions will also be made public.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: It must be painful for the journalists to report the wrongdoing of their colleagues, or sometimes it could be their supervisors in the newspapers.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The first question is, in the funding formula for SMT, will the circulation numbers be one of the KPIs or is there a KPI for them to increase the circulation because that will add pressure on them?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Two, why is it that the names of the companies involved in helping to inflate the circulation numbers are not revealed?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Is it because they are subject to Police investigation and the Minister cannot reveal that?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: In the public interest, we hope that the Ministry can get the papers to release them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Maybe I will take the second question first.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang had asked why were the names of the companies and the staff who were involved in the potential wrongdoing not made public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members will know, the matter has been referred to the Police for investigations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT has provided all the findings that the ARC submitted to the Board and this full set of findings would have already been made available to the Police.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They include the names of the companies and the people involved.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, as far as the ARC's findings were concerned, the Police have full view of it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nothing that was provided to the Police was redacted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because it is an ongoing investigation, as to who will eventually have to be held liable under the law, these things will need to take their natural course.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is for the relevant authorities, after they have completed their investigations, to determine what information to publicly disclose and when to do so, so as to not affect the outcome of their investigations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That will be something that has to be left to a later date.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang asked specifically whether circulation is part of the KPIs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A title that is being circulated in print today can be read by multiple people.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And as media move more and more online, it is not so much the circulation that matters.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The reach measures how often people come into contact with the contents of a particular title.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is reach that is more important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, the KPIs must be reached, and, in particular, digital reach.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will, in fact, also ask for specific reach indicators for vernacular groups and youths, because the funding is directed mainly in three areas: the technology upgrade; the talent development, building up the newsrooms; and, very importantly, in terms of how vernacular media continue to be safeguarded.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, the KPIs follow the thrusts of our funding objectives.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I just have a very short supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened to hear that SMT is committed to improve its accountability and its risk measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I just want to ask the Minister whether the Ministry is prepared to consider ring-fencing an amount out of the $900 million funding support for SMT, to strengthen its internal accountability and to prevent incidents from happening in the future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We expect that some of the funding will be needed for general purposes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These measures that SMT needs to take obviously require some resource allocation on their part, both in terms of the manpower as well as the management bandwidth.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We expect them to manage within the block of funding that is provided to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As far as possible, we size the funding according to the needs that are most pertinent to successful transformation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Strengthening governance is certainly a big part of it, but we also expect SMT to allocate its own resources accordingly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, for the time being, there is no specific intention to ring-fence resources for improving governance, but to expect SMT to direct resources towards improving governance.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The corresponding revenue and expenses should not have been recognised and the corresponding circulation numbers should not have been counted.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, my question is, if it was found that the X Barter Deal was not a genuine arrangement, will there be any investigation into the other media company, which was named as "X" in the report, and whether they were also inflating their numbers?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But what kind of accountability has been given to the donors and the clients who had contributed to the NIE Fund on the understanding that they were helping the underprivileged in society but were instead used to shore up the circulation figures for SPH?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Are they specifically looking to establish liability in the context that Mr Giam described?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: On the Member's second question on accountability to the donors and the other parties that made resources available to SPH Limited, the purpose of making full disclosure on the findings is precisely to allow these entities to decide if they want to take further action.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not for us to decide on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, when was the first tranche of the public funds paid out to SPH Media Trust?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Was it before or after the completion of the audit committee report?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I hope that answers the Member's question.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The investigations will have to take its full course and then a decision will be taken.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Since the revelation of this incident, is MCI keeping track of whether the international standing and the local public's confidence in SMT's products have dipped subsequent to the announcements?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And as what the Minister has shared earlier in response to Member Ang Wei Neng, are we seeing the trend of a drop in terms of the reach of their contents and their engagements with the general public at large as well?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In my engagements with SMT, they are themselves equally concerned if the level of trust that is ascribed to them by the public suffers a loss as a result of this incident.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I believe this is a key consideration why SMT has taken great pains to ensure that it has undertaken a full and thorough investigation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It took pains to make the findings public; it took pains to be quite careful about whether there was a potential offence to have been committed and they decided not to take any chances but, instead, to file a Police report.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the seriousness of this incident and its potential impact on the levels of trust that the public has in SMT and its titles, are not lost on its Board as well as the management.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is another matter that MCI would be equally concerned with and SMT knows this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Henceforth, SMT is in receipt of public funding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, its ability to be held accountable will be carefully scrutinised, both by MCI as well as by the public.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This accountability in relation to funding will include the extent to which SMT has been successful in its transformation, especially towards digital media.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will also be held accountable for maintaining trust.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, the measures that the Member talked about, not only will MCI track, SMT itself will be interested.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will rely on independent reports, such as those carried out by Reuters Institute, but we will also have our own studies to confirm what these independent resources have established as findings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Accountability to the public also extends to improving governance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you look at the media reports and also in the ARC's findings, there is a significant portion of the reports that cover governance measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, SMT is well aware that it is one thing to tell people what the findings are; it is quite another to commit to making improvements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the improvements in governance essentially are to do three things.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is to make sure that bad things do not happen again; it is to ensure that your systems for controls and contracting, pricing have to be cleaned up, made better; and the other aspect of governance that needs to be improved is also the culture – how people view these kinds of things and their willingness to tolerate them or to speak against them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MCI takes all of these matters of accountability seriously.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SMT knows it at the Board level as well as the management level.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They know that in the reviews that we will be conducting as a part of this funding arrangement, this topic will consistently come up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And we will have to satisfy ourselves that the remedies have been implemented and effort is being made to sustain trust by the public.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I think Members have asked various questions, including myself.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I just want to remind Members of the critical role that SPH Media has played, particularly recently, in the COVID-19 fight, to dispel untruths and put the right messages out there and receive certificates of commendation as well.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The level of trust, I thank the Minister for the assurance —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, can you ask your question, please?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: So, for the future findings and future commitments to accountability and building up trust, I hope that there can be periodical reports and disclosures to the public to ensure that the measures and safeguards are being put in place.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Given that there may be potential breaches of the Companies Act involved, is the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) looking at its own investigation and enforcement actions when it comes to not just the employees and ex-employees that were mentioned in the report but, potentially, also the directors of then-SPH for potential breach of fiduciary duties?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Similarly, given that it was a listed company back then, is SGX also looking at its own regulatory actions in relation to some of these misstatements of circulation and financial figures?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to whether the other agencies intend to take regulatory action, this is something for them to decide and I cannot answer on their behalf.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And if they have not done so, will the Government be asking them to look into this?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have no more information to offer to Mr Tan other than what he is able to access from the public records.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was asked by the Board to meet a set of terms of reference.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am not aware of them being asked to investigate the goings-on before that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, therefore, myself, what I can share is that, from the report, I did not see them making conclusions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I did not see them drawing conclusions for the period before that.
